reason: The text depicts the Egyptian Pharaoh actively oppressing the Hebrew people without any acknowledgment of responsibility or moral accountability for their suffering. When the Pharaoh becomes aware that the Hebrew population is growing, he responds with escalating oppression—enslaving them with taskmasters and heavy labor—rather than taking any responsibility for their welfare or condition. He frames them as a threat ('lest they multiply') rather than as people for whom leadership bears responsibility. His commands to the midwives and later to throw Hebrew infants into the Nile demonstrate a complete absence of accountability; instead, he compounds the people's suffering through deliberate, hostile actions without expressing any remorse or sense of moral obligation.
